title: Odd Even Linked List
description: Brute force to optimized: extracting into two arrays versus an in-place simultaneous two-chain leapfrog technique.

blocks.text: Given the head of a singly linked list, group all the nodes at ODD positions together, followed by all the nodes at EVEN positions (1-indexed), and return the reordered list. The first node is at position 1, considered odd.

blocks.caption: All odd-position nodes are grouped first, followed by all even-position nodes, preserving their relative order within each group

blocks.content: {"headers":["Aspect","Detail"],"rows":[["Input","The head of a singly linked list"],["Output","The head of the list, reordered so all odd-position nodes come first, followed by all even-position nodes"],["Goal","Achieve this reordering in a single pass, using O(1) extra space and preserving relative order within each group"],["Constraints","The number of nodes is in the range [0, 10^4]; -10^6 <= Node.val <= 10^6"]]}

{"headers":["Signal in the problem","Pattern it points to"],"rows":[["Nodes need to be split into two interleaved groups (odd vs even positions) and then reconnected","Building TWO separate chains simultaneously while walking the list once, then joining them at the end"],["O(1) extra space, single pass expected","In-place pointer manipulation using two \"tracking\" pointers (one per chain), rather than extracting into arrays"]]}

blocks.text: The list's nodes alternate between "odd position" and "even position" (1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, ...). All odd-position nodes should end up first (in their original relative order), followed by all even-position nodes (also in their original relative order).

blocks.title: Analogy: Splitting a Deck by Alternating Cards
blocks.text: Like dealing a shuffled-in deck of cards into two separate piles by alternating (1st card to pile A, 2nd card to pile B, 3rd card to pile A, and so on), then finally placing pile B directly on top of pile A. Each pile individually keeps its cards in the order they were dealt; only the TWO piles themselves are reordered relative to each other.

blocks.caption: Two chains (odd and even) grow simultaneously while walking the list once; the odd chain's tail is finally linked to the even chain's head

blocks.text: Before extracting values into separate arrays and rebuilding, notice that two chains (odd and even) can be grown SIMULTANEOUSLY while walking the list just once, using pointer re-linking alone.

blocks.title: Building the Intuition
blocks.text:
Observation 1: Starting two pointers, "odd" at the 1st node and "even" at the 2nd node, each one represents the current TAIL of its respective growing chain.

Observation 2: At each step, odd.next can be set directly to even.next (the node two positions ahead), correctly skipping over the in-between even node and extending the odd chain.

Observation 3: Symmetrically, even.next can be set to the (new) odd.next, extending the even chain past the in-between odd node.

Observation 4: This "leapfrog" pattern (odd skips ahead by 2, even skips ahead by 2) naturally separates the two chains in a single pass, without ever needing to know the list's length in advance.

Observation 5: The only remaining step is remembering the even chain's ORIGINAL head (before it gets modified), so it can be attached to the odd chain's final tail at the very end.
This is a two-pointer "leapfrog" technique: both chains are built simultaneously in a single pass, each pointer skipping over the other chain's in-between node.
Extract all values into two separate arrays based on their 0-indexed position's parity, then concatenate the odd-position array followed by the even-position array.

items: Walk through the list once, appending each value to an "odd" array (0-indexed even positions) or an "even" array (0-indexed odd positions), based on its index parity.
Concatenate the odd array followed by the even array to produce the final reordered result.

blocks.text: Why the code is written this way

items: 0-indexed position i corresponds to the (i+1)-th (1-indexed) node, so 1-indexed ODD positions are exactly the 0-indexed EVEN indices.
Two separate arrays keep the odd-position and even-position values cleanly separated before the final concatenation.

blocks.text: Every node is correctly classified by its position parity, and relative order within each group is naturally preserved by iterating in order.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(n), one pass to classify plus one to rebuild.
Space: O(n), for the two intermediate arrays.
Limitation: extracting into arrays ignores that the EXISTING nodes can simply be re-linked in place into two chains, then joined, achieving the same result in O(1) extra space.

blocks.title: The Optimization Journey
blocks.text: The brute force rebuilds two entirely new arrays. Instead, keep two pointers, odd and even, starting at the 1st and 2nd nodes respectively. Remember the even chain's original head. Repeatedly re-link odd.next to skip ahead 2 nodes (to the next odd-position node), and even.next likewise (to the next even-position node), advancing both. When even (or even.next) runs out, attach the remembered even-chain head directly after the odd chain's final tail.

Handle the 0 or 1 node case directly (nothing to reorder). Otherwise, initialize odd = head, even = head.next, evenHead = even. While even and even.next are non-null: set odd.next = even.next, advance odd; set even.next = odd.next, advance even. Finally, set odd.next = evenHead.
Grow the odd and even chains simultaneously in a single pass, then join the odd chain's tail to the even chain's head.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Step","Action","odd chain so far","even chain so far"],"rows":[["Setup","odd=1, even=2, evenHead=2","[1]","[2]"],["Iteration 1","odd.next=even.next(3); odd=3. even.next=odd.next(4); even=4","[1,3]","[2,4]"],["Iteration 2","even.next is null (5.next), so odd.next=even.next(5); odd=5. even.next=odd.next(null); even=null","[1,3,5]","[2,4]"],["Loop ends","even is null, stop","[1,3,5]","[2,4]"],["Join","odd.next = evenHead (2)","[1,3,5,2,4]","-"]]}

blocks.title: Final answer
blocks.text: The joined list is [1,3,5,2,4], matching the expected result.

codes.python:
def odd_even_list(head):
    if not head or not head.next:
        return head

    odd = head                                                              # odd starts at the 1st node
    even = head.next                                                        # even starts at the 2nd node
    even_head = even                                                        # remembered so it can be attached at the very end

    while even and even.next:
        odd.next = even.next                                                # skip odd past the in-between even node
        odd = odd.next
        even.next = odd.next                                                # skip even past the in-between odd node
        even = even.next

    odd.next = even_head                                                    # attach the even chain right after the odd chain
    return head


if __name__ == "__main__":
    head = ListNode(1, ListNode(2, ListNode(3, ListNode(4, ListNode(5)))))
    result = odd_even_list(head)
    values = []
    while result:
        values.append(result.val)
        result = result.next
    print(values)

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(n), a single pass through the list.
Space: O(1) extra, reusing the existing nodes.

At every point during the loop, odd.next always points to the NEXT odd-position node (correctly skipping over the in-between even node), and symmetrically for even.next. This means both chains are already correctly ordered internally by the time the loop ends; only the two chains themselves (as a whole) need joining, which the final odd.next = evenHead step accomplishes.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Case","What happens"],"rows":[["even or even.next becomes null","The loop stops; the even chain has been fully traversed and separated"],["Loop iteration","Both odd and even advance by exactly one \"slot\" in their own chain, correctly leapfrogging over the other chain's node"],["Final join","odd (now the odd chain's true tail) connects directly to evenHead, completing the reordering"]]}

items: evenHead must be saved BEFORE the loop begins, since even.next gets reassigned repeatedly during the loop, losing the original head otherwise.
The loop condition (even != null && even.next != null) correctly handles both even and odd total list lengths, stopping exactly when there are no more even-position nodes left to link.
A 0 or 1 node list is handled as a direct early return, since there is nothing meaningful to reorder.

blocks.text: When nodes need to be regrouped by an alternating pattern (odd/even position), growing two chains SIMULTANEOUSLY with a leapfrog re-linking pattern achieves the regrouping in a single pass with O(1) extra space.

items: Forgetting to save evenHead before the loop begins, losing the ability to reattach the even chain at the end.
Using the wrong loop condition (for example, checking only "even != null" without also checking "even.next != null"), causing a null pointer error when even.next is accessed.
Confusing 1-indexed "odd position" with 0-indexed array logic when translating the brute force to the optimized in-place version.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Edge case","Expected behavior"],"rows":[["Empty list or single node","Returned unchanged, since there is nothing to reorder"],["Exactly two nodes","The odd chain is just the 1st node, the even chain just the 2nd; joining them leaves the list unchanged"],["Odd total length vs even total length","Both are correctly handled by the same loop condition, since it naturally stops once even-position nodes are exhausted"]]}

items: Drawing out the "leapfrog" pointer movements on a small example (5-6 nodes) before writing any code makes the exact re-linking order much easier to get right on the first attempt.

blocks.title: If The Interviewer Says This, Think This
blocks.text: "Regroup a list by an ALTERNATING position pattern" points toward growing two separate chains simultaneously in a single pass, rather than extracting and rebuilding.

items: How would this change if positions needed to be grouped by "every 3rd node" instead of alternating? A similar simultaneous multi-chain technique could work, though tracking three (or k) chains at once adds complexity.

Can you do this while ALSO reversing each individual chain? That would require additionally re-linking each chain's internal pointers, combining this technique with the standard iterative reversal technique.

How would you verify the two chains are being built correctly without printing the whole list? Tracing just the odd and even pointers' positions after each iteration (as in the dry run) confirms the leapfrog logic directly.

A "simultaneous multi-chain" variation of general linked-list re-linking techniques, conceptually related to the interleave/weave technique used in Copy List with Random Pointer elsewhere in this category.

blocks.title: Complexity Summary
blocks.text:
Brute force: O(n) time, O(n) space.
Optimized (simultaneous two-chain leapfrog): O(n) time, O(1) space.

items: Pattern: Simultaneous two-chain leapfrog re-linking

Core Idea: Grow the odd-position and even-position chains at the same time in a single pass, each pointer skipping over the other chain's in-between node, then join the odd chain's tail to the remembered even chain's head
Time: O(n)
Space: O(1)
Most Important Observation: Both chains stay correctly ordered internally throughout the single pass; only a final join between the two whole chains is needed
Interview Difficulty: Medium
One-line memory trick: odd.next=even.next, even.next=odd.next, repeat, then odd.next=evenHead
